what: Ternium makes steel in Mexico, Argentina, Brazil and Colombia: flat steel for carmakers, appliance manufacturers and construction, with its own iron ore mining in Mexico.
customers: Carmakers, appliance manufacturers, builders and energy companies across Latin America.
money: iron ore from its Mexican mines
moat: Mills inside Mexico serving carmakers who need steel delivered daily, protected by freight costs and by the regional supply chains that nearshoring has strengthened.
risks: Steel prices set the results and have fallen from their 2021 peak
Cheap Chinese steel imports into Latin America have pressured prices
Revenue fell from $17.6B to $15.6B last year
opportunities: 9.6 times earnings and 4.2 times EBITDA with $3.1B of cash against $2.4B of debt
Analysts see about 37% upside, with 14 covering the stock
Nearshoring of manufacturing into Mexico raises steel demand close to its mills
watch: Steel shipment volumes in Mexico and the price per tonne.
